title: Position Paper: Losing our Tail – Again: On (Un)Natural Selection And Multilingual Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Synthesizing prior empirical studies on model collapse, lexical diversity metrics, and machine translation outputs to demonstrate algorithmic preferences for high-frequency words, dominant languages, and the subsequent flattening of rare, long-tailed linguistic forms.

Reviewing previous machine translation experiments that assess the disproportionate generation of masculine morphological forms (e.g., 'président') over feminine ones ('présidente') when translating from gender-neutral source text.
Analyzing literature on how dominant societal heuristics and English-encoded stereotypes propagate and 'leak' across language boundaries into typologically distant languages via multilingual LLMs.
